newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea releases financial reform draft.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea releases financial reform draft.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea on Thursday released its own draft for financial reforms, calling for a continued existence of the three financial watchdog bodies.
The release was made through the bank's public information office in the name of "all employees", but it was not clear whether the draft was approved by the bank's governor.
The finance ministry said on June 16 the Office of Bank Supervision, the Securities Supervisory Board and the Insurance Supervisory Board would be unified under the prime minister.
The Bank of Korea's release said the finance ministry's idea was aimed at keeping the government's grip of the financial industry.
It said the ministry's draft was also aimed at limiting the efficiency of the financial industry supervisory system.
Finance minister Kang Kyong-shik said earlier in a news conference the Bank of Korea's governor Lee Kyung-shick had agreed to the ministry's draft.
The release also opposed the ministry's plan to run the Monetary Board, the nation's top monetary policy-making body, independently with the central bank as an implementing body.
Currently, the board belongs to the Bank of Korea while the finance minister heads the board.
The ministry's draft stipulates that the board's chairman would be appointed by the President and would also become the governor of the central bank.
The release also said the bank's budget should continue to be supervised by the Monetary Board, whereas the ministry's plan calls for the ministry's partial control of the budget.
